fine_lines.title: Up for vs down for
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما يعني: مستعد وراغب في فعل شيء. up for أكثر شيوعاً في بريطانيا. down for عامية أكثر وأصلها أمريكي ويستخدمها الشباب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean 'happy and willing to do something'. 'Up for' is common in British English. 'Down for' is more slangy, from American English, and used by younger people.

examples.sentence: Are you up for a walk after lunch?
Pizza tonight? I'm down for that!

fine_lines.title: Talk through your hat vs off the top of my head
words: off the top of my head
fine_lines.explanation_ar: talk through your hat أن تتكلم عن شيء لا تعرفه وتقول كلاماً غير صحيح. off the top of my head أن تعطي جواباً سريعاً من الذاكرة دون تحقق، وقد يكون صحيحاً تقريباً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Talk through your hat' = speak about things you don't know, saying nonsense. 'Off the top of my head' = an honest quick answer from memory, without checking.

examples.sentence: He says he can fly a plane, but he's talking through his hat.

examples.word: off the top of my head
examples.sentence: Off the top of my head, there are about 30 students.

expressions.phrase: off the top of my head
expressions.meaning_ar: من دون تفكير طويل / من ذاكرتي مباشرة
expressions.meaning_en: without checking or thinking carefully; a quick guess
expressions.example: Off the top of my head, I think the shop closes at nine.

expressions.meaning_en: confused and not sure what to do
expressions.example: I was all at sea on my first day in the new job.

expressions.meaning_en: don't give up; keep going in a difficult time
expressions.example: The exams are nearly over - hang in there!

expressions.meaning_en: something that shows you there is a problem you must deal with
expressions.example: Failing the test was a wake-up call - now I study every day.

expressions.phrase: be up for / down for something
expressions.meaning_en: to be willing and interested in doing something
expressions.example: I'm up for a game of football. Are you down for it too?

expressions.meaning_ar: يتكلم بلا علم / يقول كلاماً فارغاً
expressions.meaning_en: to talk about something you don't know about; to talk nonsense
expressions.example: Ignore him - he's talking through his hat about cars.

expressions.meaning_en: to love something very much; it is the most important thing in your life

expressions.meaning_ar: أعرف ذلك جيداً! (أوافقك تماماً لأنني أعيش الشيء نفسه)
expressions.meaning_en: said to show you strongly agree because you have the same experience
expressions.example: 'This traffic is terrible!' - 'Tell me about it!'

grammar.title: Prepositions in fixed expressions
grammar.explanation_ar: في التعابير الاصطلاحية لا نغيّر حرف الجر: off the top of my head، at sea، in there، up for، through your hat، live for. معنى التعبير لا يُفهم من حرف الجر وحده، بل يُحفظ كوحدة واحدة.
grammar.explanation_en: In idioms, the preposition is fixed: off the top of my head, at sea, in there, up for, through your hat, live for. Learn each expression as one unit.
examples: I'm up for it. (not *I'm up to it* - that has a different meaning)
